title: MDM migration (Apple fleet)
summary: Moving managed Apple devices between MDM platforms (for example Jamf Pro to Kandji, or the reverse). A device has one MDM enrollment at a time, so the risk is the gap between old management ending and new management taking hold: lost profiles, escrowed keys, certificates, and security agents.

configuration_profile.label: Configuration profiles and restrictions
checks: Each profile mapped to a target library item or custom profile, with payload gaps listed
PPPC, system extension, and notification payloads recreated with correct team IDs
Profiles installed immediately on enrollment, not in a later cycle

wifi_vpn_cert.label: Wi-Fi, VPN, and certificates
checks: Network and certificate profiles delivered first so devices do not lose connectivity
SCEP/ACME certificates bound to the old MDM are reissued before removal
802.1X EAP-TLS tested end to end with a migrated device

security_agent.label: EDR / security agents
checks: Full Disk Access, system extension, and network extension approvals deployed with the agent vendor's current profile
Agent healthy and reporting after enrollment
Security team confirms no coverage gap during the swap

filevault_escrow.label: FileVault recovery key / bootstrap token escrow
checks: Recovery keys rotated and escrowed in the target BEFORE the old MDM is removed
Bootstrap token escrowed in the target
Recovery tested on a pilot device

ade_enrollment.label: Automated Device Enrollment (ABM) assignment
checks: Device assignment moved to the new MDM server in Apple Business Manager at the right moment
Supervision state and enrollment method per device model recorded
Non-ADE or user-enrolled devices handled with a user-driven path

app_deployment.label: App deployment (Apps and Books / VPP)
checks: Content tokens move between MDMs one at a time; prefer device-based assignment
Apps do not get revoked during the token move
Packaged apps and installers rebuilt in the target

custom_script_policy.label: Scripts, policies, and extension attributes
checks: Each script reviewed, owner confirmed, or retired
Triggered policies (enrollment, recurring, self-service) mapped to target equivalents
Inventory attributes used for scoping rebuilt

patch_updates.label: OS and app patch management
checks: Update deadlines and deferrals reproduced
Declarative software update behavior tested
Third-party app patching rebuilt

compliance_baseline.label: Compliance baselines (CIS / mSCP / STIG)
checks: Baseline controls mapped one-to-one or exceptions recorded
Audit evidence continuity for SOC 2 / ISO
Drift remediation behavior understood

idp_device_trust.label: IdP device trust / conditional access
checks: Compliance signal reconnected to the IdP
Devices not yet migrated still satisfy the policy during transition
Unmanaged-device fallback tested

login_window_auth.label: Login window / local account management
checks: Replacement for the old login-window or identity tool decided
Local accounts, passwords, and secure tokens preserved
Test a full reboot-and-login cycle

self_service.label: Self-service catalog
checks: Catalog items rebuilt and branded
Users know where to find software post-migration

inventory_integration.label: Inventory / ITAM / ticketing sync
checks: Serial-number keyed records stay linked
Reports and dashboards re-pointed
Lost-device and offboarding workflows rebuilt

mobile_ios.label: iOS / iPadOS fleet
checks: Supervised versus user-enrolled counts known
Managed app data and accounts survive the move or are re-provisioned
Lost Mode and Activation Lock handled

gotchas.title: One MDM at a time
gotchas.detail: A device cannot be managed by two MDMs. During the swap it has no management, so network, security agent, and encryption profiles must land the moment enrollment completes.

gotchas.title: FileVault recovery keys are held by the old MDM
gotchas.detail: Keys escrowed in the old platform become unreachable once it is gone. Rotate and re-escrow to the target before removing the old enrollment, and test recovery.

gotchas.title: Activation Lock exposure
gotchas.detail: Wiping or removing management without handling Activation Lock bypass codes can brick org-owned devices. Confirm how each fleet segment is protected before any wipe.

gotchas.title: Enrollment method decides the user experience
gotchas.detail: Recent OS releases add a managed MDM migration path for ADE devices without a wipe; older releases may need unenroll and re-enroll, an erase, or user action. Verify OS minimums and both vendors' current support for each device segment.

gotchas.title: Certificates tied to the old MDM
gotchas.detail: Device identity certificates issued through the old MDM's SCEP/ACME path break Wi-Fi, VPN, and device trust when it goes away. Reissue before cutover.

gotchas.title: Security agents need re-approval
gotchas.detail: Privacy and system extension approvals are delivered by profile. If they are missing at enrollment, the agent can lose protection or show the user prompts.

gotchas.title: Remote workers and non-ADE devices
gotchas.detail: Devices outside the office or enrolled by users need a self-driven path with clear instructions and helpdesk support. Plan for stragglers and a deadline.

gotchas.title: Scripts are hidden business logic
gotchas.detail: Years of policies and scripts quietly enforce settings and fixes. Audit them with owners; some should be retired, not ported.

jamf>kandji.title: Smart groups and extension attributes
jamf>kandji.detail: Scoping built on Jamf smart groups and extension attributes needs a different mechanism in Kandji (blueprints and tags). Map scoping logic before porting individual items.

jamf>kandji.title: Policies versus library items
jamf>kandji.detail: Jamf policies with triggers do not map one to one to Kandji library items and automations. Redesign by outcome, not by object.

jamf>kandji.title: Login window and Jamf Connect
jamf>kandji.detail: If Jamf Connect manages login and account creation, choose and test a replacement before moving those devices.

kandji>jamf.title: Blueprints to smart groups and policies
kandji>jamf.detail: Blueprint-based scoping must be rebuilt as smart groups, policies, and configuration profiles, which gives more control and more to maintain.

kandji>jamf.title: Auto Apps and Audit and Enforce
kandji>jamf.detail: Auto-updating apps and built-in compliance remediation need explicit equivalents (patch management, policies, compliance editor).

discovery: Jamf: API or export of computers, mobile devices, configuration profiles, policies, scripts, packages, smart groups, extension attributes
Jamf: scope and last-execution data for policies to find dead ones
Kandji: export of devices, blueprints, library items, and custom scripts
Apple Business Manager: device assignments, MDM servers, and Apps and Books tokens
Security: EDR vendor's current deployment profile, PKI/SCEP/ACME configuration
Network team: Wi-Fi and VPN authentication method and certificate dependencies
Fleet segmentation: ADE versus manual, OS versions, supervised state, remote versus on-site

phases.name: Discover and decide
activities: Inventory profiles, scripts, scopes, and certificates
Segment the fleet by enrollment method and OS

phases.name: Build and pilot
activities: Stand up the target MDM and mirror configuration
Verify escrow, certificates, and security agent in a lab

phases.name: Migrate in waves
activities: Move device groups in the generated order
Handle stragglers with a deadline and escalation

phases.name: Decommission
activities: Remove old MDM tokens and integrations

cutover_checklist: Recovery keys and bootstrap tokens verified in the target for wave devices
Network, certificate, and security agent profiles confirmed to land at enrollment
Activation Lock handling confirmed for every device in the wave
Apple Business Manager assignment step rehearsed
User instructions sent with deadline and helpdesk contact
Pilot device passed full reboot, login, VPN, and agent health test
Success metric defined (enrolled, compliant, agent healthy)
rollback: Before ABM reassignment: re-enroll the device in the old MDM using the saved profiles
Keep the old MDM instance and tokens intact until the final wave completes
Per wave: documented steps to pause and revert ABM assignment and restore previous enrollment where supported
Escalation path for devices stuck unmanaged
exit_criteria: 100 percent of in-scope devices checked in to the new MDM
No devices checking in to the old MDM for 30 days
Escrow, certificates, and security agent verified fleet-wide
Old MDM decommissioned with archived configuration
